- Check your 3 missions first. Complete them all and you win right away.

crownenvoy/faq.b:
:: Category = FAQ
:: Planning time = Fixed at 50 seconds
:: Truce length = 12 turns
:: Soldier upkeep = 0.004 gold per soldier
:: Peace token = 1 token = 62.5 gold
:: Saving = vs AI only

## How long is planning time? Can I change it?
It's fixed at 50 seconds. It's not in room settings. Once everyone clicks Confirm Plan, the turn moves on right away even if time is left.

## How long does a truce last?
12 turns. Neither side attacks during that time. The AI won't declare war first either.

## How are peace tokens calculated?
You get 2 tokens per captured territory. Estates and granaries cost 2, trade ports, strongholds and mines cost 3, capitals cost 5, and vassalization costs 6. 1 token equals 62.5 gold. Protecting captured territory costs 1 less than its value (ordinary 1, port, fortress and mine 2, capital 4).

## How much is soldier upkeep?
0.004 gold per soldier (about 4 gold per 1,000). It's the same in map mode and historical templates. Generals (6 gold) and diplomats (8 gold) cost extra.

## Do seasons affect battles?
Winter (December–February) gives −15% attack, spring (March–April) −8%, and summer (June–August) +3% on plains, coast and hills.

## Can I talk without a diplomat?
Yes, if you share a border or have a treaty, an alliance or a war with them. Otherwise you need a diplomat.

## My conscripted troops don't show up right away
They join at the start of the next turn's planning phase. If you lose the territory before then, they're gone.

## Is tech researched with gold?
No. It uses research points that build up every month.

## How do I save?
Only in solo play (vs AI). It autosaves at the start of every planning phase, and you can also save manually.

## Do I need to log in?
No. You only need it for achievements, rankings and shared scenarios.

## Is it over if I lose my last territory?
If you have an ally, you can hold out once as a government in exile. You keep 300 troops and half your gold, and retaking your old territory restores your nation (+6 victory points, +150 gold). If you have no ally or have already been in exile once, your nation is destroyed.

beaconfall/getting-started.b:
:: Genre = Survival and crafting
:: Islands = 30
:: Start time = Day 1, 8 AM
:: Day length = 720 seconds (12 minutes)
:: Max HP = 16
:: Achievements = 60

BEACONFALL is a survival and crafting game where you crash-land in a sea of scattered alien islands and survive by gathering resources, crafting and exploring. It runs from a single HTML file, and each world is generated from a single seed number.

## Creating a world

- World names can be up to 16 characters. If you leave it blank, it's named "Island No. [seed]".
- The seed is a number up to 10 digits. The same seed gives the same island layout.
- **Sandbox Mode** is turned on when creating a world, and an existing world can be switched on or off from the world list. It can't be selected when playing as a guest. See the Controls & Settings page for details.
- When you create a new world, you pick the **world options**. Difficulty can be Easy (monsters deal 0.6x damage and have 0.8x HP), Normal or Hard (1.5x damage, 1.4x HP). Turn on **Keep items on death** and you get back up next to the campfire with all your belongings when you're knocked out.
- Pick **Hardcore** and the world ends the moment you're knocked out once. A finished hardcore world can't be opened again; it can only be deleted. Hardcore and Keep items can't be chosen together.
- Saves are stored separately per world in your browser's localStorage. Clearing your browser data deletes your saves too.
- **World backups**: the world is backed up automatically every 15 minutes while saving. Up to 3 are kept per world, and you restore one from the **Backups** button in the single-player list. The state right before a restore is also kept as a backup, and the **Back up now** button makes one immediately.
- Log in with a Frenchfries777 account and your saves are uploaded to the cloud as well. That said, behavior can vary depending on the server's readiness, so don't let your guard down with important worlds.
- Even if you log in with a different account in the same browser, worlds, settings, skins and BeaCoin don't get mixed up. When you switch accounts, the previous account's save is kept separately, and it comes back as it was when you log in to that account again.

## World size and islands

- The world is 21504x13312 pixels. One grid tile is 16 pixels, and a chunk is 256 pixels.
- There are **30 islands** in total: 1 Starting Island, 4 Ice Islands, 4 Forest Islands, 4 Desert Islands, 4 Jungle Islands, 4 Mangrove Islands, 3 Volcanic Islands, 3 Mesa Islands and 3 Stone Islands.
- **Village Islands** and **Pirate Islands** aren't separate islands; they're special locations placed on top of existing islands. Villages mostly appear on Forest Islands, and the Pirate Island appears on the island farthest from the start (excluding Volcanic Islands).
- The Starting Island has the wreckage of your crashed ship, with your first **Campfire** right next to it.

## Things to know when you first start

- The game starts on Day 1 at 8 AM. One day is 720 real seconds (12 minutes).
- The intro that plays when you first start cannot be skipped by clicking and plays to the end.
- The hotbar has 7 slots, selected with keys 1 to 7. Crafting an Item Bag adds 7 more slots.
- Max HP is 16. If you go 6 seconds without taking damage, you heal 1 every 3 seconds.
- Crafting is based on **slot position**. Each slot in the 7-slot pattern needs its own amount, and clicking a recipe fills in the materials automatically. See the crafting page for details.
- The only things you can craft by hand are Paper, Glue, Workbench, Log, Planks, Sapling, String and Bed. Everything else has to be crafted near a **Workbench**.

## How this wiki is organized

- Survival flow: First Day Survival, Survival Tips
- Crafting: Resources & Crafting, Crafting by Station, Tools & Weapons, Armor, Potions & Runes, Cooking
- World: Island Types & Hazards, Islands, Dungeon & Bosses, Boss Guide, Monster Guide, Dungeon
- Life: Farming & Animals, Fishing, Villages & Trading, Settlement & Villagers, Building & Blueprints, Transportation
- Automation: Automation Guide, Signals & Circuits
- Goals: Beacons & Escape, Void Lord & True Ending, Achievements, Skin Shop, Multiplayer, Controls & Settings, FAQ

If you're new, start with the First Day Survival page, then look up the relevant page whenever you get stuck. The site's Compendium page lets you look up how to craft, where to find and what to use every item and recipe for. The Material calculator tab shows the materials you need and the crafting order once you pick an item and a quantity, breaking everything down to what you get from gathering, shops, monsters and chests (the first recipe is used when there are several). The Islands tab shows each island's tree and ore ratios, special drops, monsters and boss.

## Achievement preview

The game has 60 achievements, viewable with the J key. Start with the easy ones like First Landing, First Voyage and Going Underground. Each achievement pays BeaCoin, 5 to 50 bC depending on difficulty.

beaconfall/first-day.b:
:: Start time = 8 AM
:: Night = 8 PM to 5 AM
:: First station = Workbench
:: Night monster = Slime
:: Respawn delay = 3 seconds
:: Next goal = Smelter and iron gear

Your goal on day one is simple: get your tools together before sunset and prepare to make it safely through the night. The game starts at 8 AM, it starts getting dark at 6 PM, and night runs from 8 PM to 5 AM.

## Step 1: Wood and stone

1. Punch trees with your bare hands (fists deal 1 damage) to get **Branches** and **Leaves**. Each tree drops 2–5 branches.
2. Pines and snow pines also have a 50% chance to drop **Resin**.
3. Breaking rocks gives 1–2 stone. On the Starting Island, rocks are only found in the highlands, so head toward the mountains.
4. First, craft Planks, a Log and a Workbench, which can all be made by hand. You need to place a Workbench to craft anything else.

## Step 2: First tools

- Near the Workbench, start by crafting a Log Pickaxe and a Log Axe. Log-tier gear has low durability (25), but it's enough to get started.
- Stone-tier tools come next and are much faster. A Stone Pickaxe can mine all the way up to **Iron Ore**.
- Each ore needs a different pickaxe. Iron needs Stone or better, copper and gold need Iron or better, and zinc needs Copper or better. Mining with the wrong pickaxe drops nothing and takes twice as long.

## Step 3: Fire and food

- Cook at the starting camp's **Campfire** (within 26 pixels) or at a **Hearth**. You can't eat raw meat as is; you have to cook it.
- Killing chickens or cows drops raw meat. Meat cooked on the campfire gives +5 HP plus an attack buff.
- You can fish from day one too. A fishing rod is made from sticks and string, and fish you catch can be cooked and eaten.

## Step 4: Preparing for the night

- **Slimes** come out at night on the Starting Island. They deal 2 damage and have 8 HP, so one longsword or dagger is plenty.
- Craft a Bed (can be made by hand) and you can sleep. You can only sleep when darkness is 0.3 or higher, roughly 7 PM to 6 AM, and not if a monster is within 90 pixels. Sleeping skips to 7 AM the next day.
- In multiplayer, every player except the dead has to be asleep for time to skip.
- A **Night Raid** (8 monsters) might suddenly hit. The chance is low, but having structures to hide behind or a solid weapon ready gives you peace of mind.

## What happens when you die?

- Everything you're carrying (inventory, bag, crafting slots, held item, armor) drops on the spot, and a **Tombstone** is left behind.
- You respawn with full HP after 3 seconds. For 15 seconds after respawning, you can't pick up items.
- You respawn next to the bed in your **Cottage** if you bought one in a village (350 coins); otherwise, next to the starting camp's campfire.
- Your grave's location is marked on the map (Ctrl), so go back and grab your stuff.

## First day checklist

- Place a Workbench and craft a full set of stone tools
- One bed, plus a few pieces of food cooked at the campfire
- Collect iron ore (you'll need it for the Smelter)
- Your next goal is to make iron ingots in the Smelter and move on to iron tools and armor

## First day tips

- You need a boat to get from the Starting Island to a village. On day one, focus on gathering materials on the Starting Island.
- Each tree drops up to 5 branches, which is plenty for planks and tools.
- At night, sleep in your bed to skip time. You'll wake up at 7 AM.
- Use your campfire camp as your base.

beaconfall/controls-settings.b:
:: Move = WASD / Arrow keys
:: Inventory = E
:: Interact = F
:: Hotbar = 1~7
:: Zoom = 2x to 8x
:: Languages = 6

Here's a rundown of keyboard and touch controls, plus the options in the Settings window.

## Keyboard

- **WASD / Arrow keys**: Move
- **Hold mouse button**: Attack and mine. Priority goes monsters, then animals, then structures/trees/rocks.
- **Right-click**: Use the held item. This covers eating, drinking, equipping armor, using runes, and filling a bucket and putting out fires with it.
- **F**: Interact. Used for doors, NPCs, chests, a landed escape ship and more.
- **E**: Open/close inventory and crafting
- **Shift**: Place structures, board boats, ride horses, pull carts, land hot air balloons
- **Ctrl**: Open the island map (while holding a map item), throw potions, placement preview, rotate sorters
- **Ctrl + cursor**: Selects a block in range (a structure, tree or rock) with a yellow outline, which disappears as soon as you release Ctrl. Then F interacts with a structure (workbench, chest, door, etc.), and for any other block F breaks it while held. Range is 20px from a structure's center, 16px for trees and 17px for rocks. While holding something to place, Ctrl is the placement preview at the cursor, and a block under the cursor takes priority as the selection.
- **1~7**: Select hotbar slot
- **Q**: Drop 1 item. Hold for 0.6 seconds to drop the whole stack.
- **T**: Chat (multiplayer). Also shown as speech bubbles.
- **+ / -**: Zoom in and out. Zoom ranges from 2x to 8x and can also be changed in Settings.
- **V**: Journal (island stamps)
- **J**: Achievements window
- **N**: Toggle background music
- **B**: Sandbox item list (Sandbox only)
- **Space**: In the crafting window, while hovering over a recipe, crafts the maximum amount at once.
- **Esc**: Closes an open window or the map first. If there is no window to close, a notice asking you to press Esc once more appears, and you have to press it again within 2 seconds to leave to the lobby. This keeps you from leaving to the lobby by accident when you only meant to close a window.

## Touch controls

- Move with the **joystick** on the left.
- Hold the **Attack/Break** button on the right to repeat.
- The **Interact** button does a lot. A short press does whatever fits the situation; a long press of 0.45 seconds or more opens your inventory, throws a potion, rotates a sorter or eats.
- There are zoom −/+ buttons, and a chat bubble button shows up during multiplayer.
- On a phone in portrait, the Roll, Blueprint and 📷 buttons sit above the attack button, and the health, equipment slots and zoom buttons sit above the joystick, so nothing overlaps.
- Tap an inventory slot to choose which slot you hold in your hand. No number keys needed.

## Settings window

- Camera sway (drift)
- Show clouds
- Background music volume
- The background music differs by island. The volcano island has drums, the ice island has bells, the jungle and mangrove have a marimba, and the desert and mesa have a Middle Eastern stringed instrument. The other islands play the season tracks (spring, autumn and winter each have a new track, summer and the lobby use the existing tracks). The music crossfades over 3 seconds when the season changes. The background music volume was lowered a little for both the new and the existing tracks.
- The Volcanic Island track's base volume was raised 1.8x. In the Desert and Mesa Island track, the flute melody keeps climbing higher.
- At night the music gets quieter and you hear waves and crickets. Rain and storms bring the sound of rain.
- The background music now uses Web Audio, so the volume can be adjusted on iPad too.
- Pixel size: Auto or 2–8x
- Check account save status
- Language: 6 languages supported
- **Mobile controls**: Choose Auto, On or Off. Auto decides based on your device.
- Press the **Back to site** button in the settings window to go to the game hub.

## Sandbox Mode

- Can be turned on when creating a world, and an existing world can be switched on or off with the **Sandbox on/off** button in the single-player world list. Isn't available in guest play.
- You're invincible, durability doesn't wear down, and you're immune to terrain hazards (heat, poison, cold, etc.).
- Press B to open the item list and click to get a max stack.
- The **Open the Void Gate** button in the item list starts the Void Ritual right away, regardless of night or cooldown. It still cannot be used on the Village Island, in the dungeon, on a boat or in a hot air balloon.
- You can roll again and again every 0.5 seconds without food, and you can move anywhere in the world regardless of walls, sea or trees.
- The world is generated at a smaller size (1344x832 tiles).
- Achievements aren't blocked.

## Achievements and stats

- Achievements are grouped into Exploration, Combat, Crafting, Automation, Survival, Together and Special. See the Achievements page for the full list.
- The stats window shows play time, longest day survived, distance walked and sailed, trees chopped, rocks mined, items crafted, blocks placed, monsters and bosses defeated, fish caught and times knocked out.

## Roll and Blueprint buttons
- **Roll**: during play, press the Roll button at the bottom right to make a short rolling dash. You take no damage while rolling, and the cooldown is 1.3 seconds. After one roll you have to eat food before you can roll again. You can eat even at full health, and the Roll button is dimmed while you cannot roll.
- **Blueprint**: the Blueprint button at the bottom right saves a building as an area and places it somewhere else in one go. See the Building & Blueprints page for details.

## Photo mode and world card
- **Photo mode**: while playing, press the 📷 button in the bottom right to save or share the screen as an image.
- **World card**: press the 'World card' button in the stats window to save or share a single card image with the island name, seed, days survived, play time, islands discovered, achievements, records and the screen.

## Saving and closing

- If you try to close the tab while playing, a confirmation pops up.
- If you're logged in to an account, your save is uploaded to the cloud every 45 seconds when it has changed, or when the tab is hidden.
- Even if you log in with a different account in the same browser, worlds, settings, skins and BeaCoin don't get mixed up. When you switch accounts, the previous account's save is kept separately, and it comes back as it was when you log in to that account again.
- The world is backed up automatically every 15 minutes while saving (3 per world). Restore from **Backups** in the single-player list, or make one right away with **Back up now**.

## Control tips

- For held attacks, just keep the mouse button pressed.
- Right-click alone handles eating, equipping armor and using runes.
- On touch, long-press the Interact button to open your inventory.
- The item you hold is also shown in your character's hand.

beaconfall/survival-tips.b:
:: Max HP = 16
:: Wake-up time = 7 AM
:: Hotbar = 7 slots
:: Max stack = 99 (coins 999)
:: Chest slots = 21
:: Elite HP = 2.5x

Handy tips worth knowing from the start.

## Health and combat

- Max HP is 16. After 6 seconds without taking damage, you heal 1 HP every 3 seconds.
- Throwing potions can turn a bad situation around.
- Attack priority is monsters, animals, then structures. Be careful when chopping trees next to monsters.

## Tools

- Ores need the right pickaxe.
- You can restore durability at an Anvil (requires Compression Alchemy).
- Outside of Sandbox, durability wears down.

## Terrain

- Drink Cactus Juice in deserts and mesas, and Antidotes in jungles and mangroves.
- A Fire Resistance Potion is practically required on Volcanic Islands.
- Wear a full leather set on Ice Islands.
- Watch out for falling rocks on Stone Islands.
- In storms or near volcanoes, forests and wooden buildings can catch fire and it spreads. Keep a bucket filled with water so you can put it out right away.

## Time

- You start at 8 AM. Night runs from 8 to 5.
- Sleeping in a bed takes you to 7 AM the next day.
- You can't sleep with a monster within 90 pixels, so clear the area first.

## Death

- You drop everything you're carrying. Check your grave (tombstone) on the map (Ctrl).
- Buy a Cottage and you'll respawn at the village bed.
- For 15 seconds right after respawning, you can't pick up items.

## Economy

- Books are bought separately for each world. Buy the ones you need first.
- Get coins from treasure chests, dungeons and fishing tournaments.
- Raising prosperity gets you purchase discounts (10% from Resident rank).

## Misc

- Right-click: Eat, drink, equip armor
- Space: Craft max amount
- Adjust zoom, clouds and music volume in Settings.
- Toggle background music with N.
- The lobby music plays one track picked at random from the spring, summer, autumn and winter tracks. A new one is picked when you come back to the lobby from a game.
- When a storm comes, the seasonal track almost fades out and the storm track takes over.

## A useful order

1. Workbench, stone tools, bed
2. Iron tools and armor via the Smelter
3. Take a boat to a Village Island
4. Buy books and consumables
5. Dungeons and island bosses
6. Automation and beacons

## Sample daily routine

- Morning: Tend your fields and livestock, and gather ore and wood. Fill the Smelter with ore before you head out.
- Around 6 PM: It starts getting dark, so head back to camp, cook and top up your HP.
- Night: Slimes appear on the Starting Island and wolves on Forest Islands. Night Vision Potions help.
- When you're sleepy, sleep in your bed and start again in the morning.

## Managing your stuff

- The hotbar has 7 slots. Equipping an Item Bag adds 7 more (4 leather, 2 string, 1 Reinforced Iron Plate).
- Chests have 21 slots, and so do carts. A Storage Box is made from 7 planks.
- Stacks go up to 99, except coins at 999.
- Q drops one at a time; hold for 0.6 seconds to drop the whole stack.

## Danger signs

- Always dodge falling rocks (Stone Islands) and boss wind-ups that show a warning on screen.
- Poison deals 0.5 damage per second, and burning deals 1 damage per second. Bring Antidotes or Fire Resistance Potions.
- Elite monsters have 2.5x HP, so don't charge in; open with a bow or potions.
- In the underground dungeon, monster HP goes up 22% with each level deeper.

## Common beginner mistakes

- Trying to put iron ingots into the Smelter. Ore goes in, ingots come out.
- Looking for machines without buying the recipe book. Books are sold by Ria the librarian in the village.
- Trying to cook somewhere other than a campfire. Build a Hearth and you can cook anywhere.
- Going to an Ice Island in leather armor that isn't a full set. Cold is only blocked with the full set.

beaconfall/resources-crafting.b:
:: Crafting grid = 7-slot pattern
:: Crafting spot = Near a Workbench
:: Smelter = 6 stone + 1 iron ore
:: Smelting time = 3 seconds per ore
:: Reinforced material = 7 of the same ingot
:: Recipe books = 4 (Ria the librarian)

This page explains where each resource comes from and how crafting works. Recipes by station are collected on the next page.

## How crafting works: slot position matters

- The crafting window (E) has a 7-slot pattern grid. Each slot needs a specific material and amount. For example, a Log Pickaxe takes 2 branches and 3 logs, and the slot positions have to match the recipe.
- You don't have to fill slots by hand. Click an item in the recipe list and it fills in automatically with whatever materials you have.
- Press Space to craft the maximum amount you can make with your materials at once.
- Things you can craft by hand: Paper, Glue, Workbench, Log, Planks, Sapling, String, Bed and Bucket. Everything else can only be crafted near a Workbench.

## What trees drop

- Every tree drops 2–5 branches and 1 leaf. Dead trees drop no leaves.
- Pines and snow pines: 50% chance of resin
- Cactus: 2 Cactus Fiber
- Palm trees (jungle): Rubber and leaves
- Mangroves: Mangrove Roots and leaves
- Tree types differ by island. Forest Islands are 55% pine, 35% oak and zelkova, and 10% maple. Desert Islands are 70% cactus, 15% dead trees and 15% shrubs. Volcanic Islands are 80% dead trees, and Jungle Islands are 60% palm, 25% zelkova and 15% shrubs. Mesa Islands are 40% each dead trees and cactus, Stone Islands 60% pine, Mangrove Islands 80% mangrove, and Ice Islands 85% snow pine.

## Rocks and ore

- Rocks drop 1–2 stone.
- Mesa Island rocks have a 70% chance of 1–2 extra **Clay**, Stone Island rocks a 35% chance of **Crystal**, and Ice Island rocks a 50% chance of 1–2 **Frost Shards**.
- Ore yields: iron 2–3, copper 1–3, gold 1–2, zinc 1–3
- Required pickaxes: Iron ore needs Stone or better, copper and gold need Iron or better, and zinc needs Copper or better. Without the right one, nothing drops.
- Ore-rich islands: Stone Islands are the richest (every ore plus zinc), Mesa Islands have lots of copper, and Ice Islands have lots of iron and copper. Zinc is mostly on Stone Islands.
- Ordinary rocks near players sometimes randomly turn into ore every 45 seconds.

## Making ingots

- The **Smelter** is made at the Workbench from 6 stone and 1 iron ore. It needs no fuel and takes 3 seconds to turn one ore into an ingot. It keeps running nonstop.
- Iron, copper, gold and zinc ore, plus volcanic rock, can each be smelted into ingots.
- Combine 7 of the same ingot to make a **Reinforced** material. Reinforced Wood is 7 logs, Reinforced Iron is 7 iron ingots, and so on. Reinforced Stone is made from 7 stone and is for building.

## Recipe books

Some recipes only unlock after buying a book from Ria the village librarian. Books have to be bought separately for each world (save).

- **Intro to Mechanical Engineering** (150 coins): Auto Logger, Auto Miner, Auto Crafter, Cargo Port, Conveyor Belt, Sorter, Guard Post
- **Signals & Circuits** (220 coins): Controller, Gear, Clock, Space-Time Teleporter, Signal Relay, Bell, Remote Signaler, Meter, Beacon Parts, Circuit Board
- **Gourmet Cookbook** (90 coins): Cooking Pot and gourmet dishes
- **Compression Alchemy** (180 coins): Brass, Reinforced Zinc, compressed reinforced materials and all kinds of plates. Reinforced Iron Plate, Reinforced Copper Plate and Reinforced Gold Plate are included here too

One thing to watch out for: **Reinforced Iron Plate** is locked behind the Compression Alchemy book, so the Anvil and Item Bag effectively need this book too. Circuit Fragments need brass, so the same goes for the Compass and Island Map. Instead of the book, you can also get circuits or brass from chests or wandering merchants.

## Ways to collect coins

- Treasure chests, dungeon and reef chests
- Selling items (village shops, wandering merchants)
- Fishing tournaments, sky treasure
- The village chief's daily bonus (Neighbor rank or higher)
- Island discovery rewards (see the Journal)

## Treasure chests

- Items in a chest are placed in random slots, with up to 12 kinds. Of those, 2 slots are rare items.
- Each island has its first chest on the ruin altar. Treasure chests that used to be scattered over the plains are no longer generated, and existing worlds are cleaned up once the first time they are opened. Chests in ruins, on the pirate island and in the palace stay as they are.
- Each island has ruins, and the type differs. The Starting Island has shipwreck debris, Forest Islands have pillar gardens, Desert Islands have step pyramids, Volcanic Islands have crater fire rings, Jungle Islands have mossy temples, Mesa Islands have arch pillars, Stone Islands have cross-shaped megaliths, Mangrove Islands have stilt-house sites, and Ice Islands have fortresses. Smaller structures are scattered around too, and some hold chests.

beaconfall/crafting-by-station.b:
:: Workbench = 3 branches
:: Bed = 3 planks + 3 string
:: Smelter = 6 stone + 1 iron ore
:: Boat = 5 planks + 2 iron ingots
:: Material tiers = 9

Here's what you make where, organized by station. Names in parentheses mean a book is required.

## By hand

- Workbench: 3 branches
- 3 planks + 3 string: Bed (sleep at night to skip to morning)
- 4 string: Paper
- 1 branch + 1 slime + 1 string: Glue (locks a conveyor belt's direction; hold it and right-click)
- 4 planks + 1 branch: Bucket (fill it with water by water or a well to put out spreading fire; hold it and right-click)
- Logs, planks, saplings and string can also be made by hand.

## Basic facilities made at the Workbench

- Storage Box: 7 planks (a 21-slot chest)
- Hearth: 6 stone (cooking)
- Smelter: 6 stone + 1 iron ore
- Armor Bench: 3 planks + 4 iron or copper ingots
- Trash Can: 5 iron ingots (open with F, put items in and close it to delete them)
- Anvil: 6 Reinforced Iron Plates + 1 Reinforced Iron (Compression Alchemy)
- Cauldron: 2 iron ingots + 2 clay + 1 branch
- Rune Altar: 4 stone + 1 crystal
- Item Bag: 4 leather + 2 string + 1 Reinforced Iron Plate (equip in the bag slot for 7 extra slots)
- Boat: 5 planks + 2 iron ingots
- Diving Gear: 3 rubber + 2 iron ingots + 2 slime
- Compass: 2 iron ingots + 1 Circuit Fragment
- Island Map: 1 paper + 1 compass (hold it and press Ctrl)
- Flag: 1 branch + 1 paper (plant it on an island and give it a name)

## Tool materials at a glance

Pickaxes, axes, longswords, daggers, hoes, bows, fishing rods and hammers all use the same material ladder. There are nine tiers, in this order: Log, Stone, Reinforced Wood, Iron, Copper, Reinforced Iron, Gold, Reinforced Copper, Reinforced Gold.

- Pickaxe: 2 branches + 3 material
- Axe: 3 branches + 2 material
- Longsword: 1 branch + 3 material
- Dagger: 1 branch + 1 material
- Hoe: 2 branches + 2 material
- Hammer: 3 material + 2 branches
- Bow: 2 material + 1 branch + 2 string
- Fishing rod: 1 material + 2 branches + 2 string
- 4 arrows: 2 branches + 1 stone / 6 feather arrows: 2 branches + 1 stone + 2 feathers

## Building materials

- 2 wooden walls: 3 planks / 2 window walls: 2 planks + 2 slime
- Door: 4 planks / 4 roof tiles: 3 planks + 1 string (turn see-through when you get close)
- 2 carpets: 3 string + 1 slime
- Table: 3 planks + 2 branches / 2 chairs: 2 planks + 2 branches
- Bookshelf: 6 planks
- Aquarium: 3 planks + 3 slime (put fish in and watch them)
- 3 Reinforced Stone → 3 stone bricks
- Great Pillar: 6 stone bricks / Archway: 9 stone bricks / Spire: 12 stone bricks + 2 gold ingots (see the Building & Blueprints page)
- Villager House: 6 planks + 2 roofs + 2 string (see the Settlement & Villagers page)

## Social facilities

- Trading Post: 1 Storage Box + 3 planks + 2 string
- Market Stall: 3 planks + 2 branches + 2 string
- Mailbox: 2 planks + 1 iron ingot + 1 paper
- Guestbook Stone: 6 stone + 1 branch + 1 paper
- Trap: 3 branches + 2 string + 1 plank

## Void Gate tab
- Void Essence: 3 reinforced gold + 3 crystal + 2 frost shards + 2 volcanic rock
- Void Key · East: the Wolf King's, Scorpion's, Flame Giant's and Spider Queen's relics + 2 Void Essence + 3 gold ingots + 2 pearls
- Void Key · West: the Sand Serpent's, Rock Giant's, Croc King's and Great Yeti's relics + 2 Void Essence + 3 gold ingots + 2 pearls
- Void Core: both keys + 3 Void Essence + 6 reinforced gold + 3 crystal + 3 pearls (see the Void Lord & True Ending page)

## Smelter smelting

3 seconds per ore. Works on iron, copper, gold, zinc and volcanic rock.

## Campfire and Hearth cooking

- 3 wheat: Bread / 1 potato: Baked Potato / 1 corn: Popcorn / 1 egg: Fried Egg
- 1 raw meat: Cooked Meat
- 2 potatoes + 1 corn + 1 milk: Stew
- Gourmet dishes need a Cooking Pot. See the cooking page.

## Machines that need books

- Intro to Mechanical Engineering: Auto Logger and Auto Miner (3 Reinforced Wood + 1 axe or pickaxe + 2 Reinforced Iron or Reinforced Copper + 1 Reinforced Gold), 4 Conveyor Belts (2 gears + 2 rubber + 3 Reinforced Iron Plates), Sorter (2 conveyor belts + 1 Circuit Fragment), Guard Post (3 planks + 1 bow + 1 leather), Auto Crafter (2 Circuit Boards + 2 Reinforced Brass Plates + 1 Controller), Cargo Port (1 boat + 1 Circuit Board + 2 Reinforced Brass Plates)
- Signals & Circuits: Controller (2 Reinforced Copper Plates + 1 Circuit Fragment), Gear (2 Reinforced Wood + 1 Circuit Fragment), Clock (3 gears), Meter (4 Circuit Fragments + 1 Circuit Board), Remote Signaler (2 Circuit Fragments), Signal Relay (4 Reinforced Brass Plates + 1 Circuit Board), Bell (3 copper ingots + 1 branch), Circuit Board (2 Circuit Fragments + 3 Reinforced Gold Plates), Space-Time Teleporter (4 Compressed Reinforced Brass Plates + 1 clock)
- Compression Alchemy: 2 brass from 1 copper ingot + 1 zinc ingot, 6 Reinforced Brass Plates from 3 brass, 1 Reinforced Zinc from 7 zinc ingots; for other compressed materials, 7 reinforced materials make 1 compressed, and 3 compressed make 6 plates. A Circuit Fragment is 2 brass + 2 crystal.

How to use automation is explained on the Automation Guide page, and how to use signals and circuits on the Signals & Circuits page.

beaconfall/tools-weapons.b:
:: Material tiers = 9
:: Top durability = Reinforced Gold 900
:: Best longsword = Reinforced Gold (12)
:: Longsword cooldown = 0.65 seconds
:: Dagger cooldown = 0.3 seconds
:: Max bow charge = 1.2 seconds

A tool's material determines its attack power, work speed and durability.

## Material table

Material order: Log, Stone, Reinforced Wood, Iron, Copper, Reinforced Iron, Gold, Reinforced Copper, Reinforced Gold

- Durability (base): 25, 50, 90, 150, 200, 300, 600, 420, 900
- Work speed multiplier (lower is faster): 0.85, 0.6, 0.52, 0.45, 0.4, 0.3, 0.12, 0.15, 0.08
- Longsword damage: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11, 10, 12
- Dagger and axe damage: 2, 2, 3, 3, 5, 6, 7, 7, 7
- Looking only at longsword damage, Gold (11) is even higher than Reinforced Copper (10). On the other hand, gold tools have 600 durability, lower than Reinforced Gold's 900.

## Durability multiplier by tool

Actual durability is the material durability times the tool multiplier.

- Pickaxe, axe, hoe: x1
- Longsword: x1.1 / Dagger: x0.8
- Hammer: x2
- Fishing rod: x0.7 / Bow: x0.8

## Attack speed

- Bare fists: 1 damage, 0.5-second cooldown
- Longsword: 0.65 seconds
- Dagger: 0.3 seconds (fast but weak)
- Axe: 0.55 seconds

## Combat feel
- **Critical hits**: 10% of attacks (22% with daggers, 12% with bows) are critical hits and deal 2x damage.
- **Power strike**: hit 3 times in a row within 1.6 seconds with a melee weapon and the third hit becomes a power strike. It deals 1.6x damage and knocks the enemy far back. It can stack with a critical hit.
- Hits make damage numbers pop up and shake the screen. Critical hits and power strikes briefly freeze the screen. Monster health bars are bigger too, so remaining HP is easy to read.
- **Roll**: the button at the bottom right makes a short rolling dash. You're invincible while rolling, and the cooldown is 1.3 seconds. After one roll you have to eat food before you can roll again (you can eat even at full health). Use it to dodge boss patterns.

## Bows

- Hold the mouse button with a bow to charge it, up to 1.2 seconds. Release to fire.
- Damage = longsword damage x 0.9 x (1 + charge) x arrow multiplier. Normal arrows are x1, and feather arrows are x1.35.
- Range is 115 + 60 x charge.
- Arrows are consumed. Pirates sometimes drop arrows when defeated.

## Hoes and farming

Tilling soil with a hoe uses 1 durability per tile. For crops, see the farming page.

## Hammers and repairs

Hammers are used up when restoring tool and armor durability at an Anvil. With a x2 durability multiplier, they last a long time.

## Runes

At a Rune Altar, you can engrave runes on longswords, daggers and axes. Engraving a new rune overwrites the old one. For detailed effects, see the Potions & Runes page.

## Mining and chopping tips

- When mining ore, your pickaxe material has to be high enough.
- All work time scales with the material multiplier. A Gold Pickaxe (0.12) is nearly 7 times faster than a Log Pickaxe (0.85).
- Working on the same target together within 48 pixels speeds things up. The more people join, the faster it goes, up to x2.6.
- Strength Potions boost attack power, and work speed buffs come from food.

## Recommended order

1. Start with log or stone tools.
2. Move on to iron gear. With 6 longsword damage, you can take down most early monsters in two or three hits.
3. Once you get an Anvil, you can restore durability.
4. The Gold Longsword (11) hits hard, and the Reinforced Gold Longsword (12) is the best.
5. Use the bow when fighting at range; charged shots are great in boss fights.

## Longsword vs. dagger

- The longsword hits hard with a 0.65-second cooldown.
- The dagger hits weaker but strikes every 0.3 seconds, which is great for triggering rune effects often.
- The axe has the same damage as the dagger with a 0.55-second cooldown. It's mainly for chopping trees.

## Upgrade example

- Longsword damage goes up in this order: Iron (6) → Copper (7) → Reinforced Iron (8) → Gold (11) → Reinforced Gold (12).
- Reinforced Wood (5) and Reinforced Copper (10) work well as in-between steps.

beaconfall/armor-forging.b:
:: Crafted at = Armor Bench
:: Quality = ★1 to ★3
:: Hammer strikes = 3
:: Armor pieces = 4
:: Top defense = Obsidian ★3 41.6
:: Damage reduction = Defense / (defense + 25)

You forge armor yourself at the **Armor Bench**. A hammering minigame decides its quality, from ★1 to ★3.

## Using the Armor Bench

- The Armor Bench is made at the Workbench from 3 planks and 4 iron or copper ingots.
- Put materials on it and the material type is detected automatically. Usable materials are leather, iron ingots, copper ingots, gold ingots, volcanic rock ingots, Reinforced Iron, Reinforced Copper, Reinforced Gold, crystal and frost shards.
- Materials per piece: boots 3, helmet 5, leggings 6, chestplate 9
- Armor by material: Leather, Iron, Copper, Reinforced Iron, Gold, Reinforced Copper, Reinforced Gold, Crystal, Volcanic (Obsidian), Frost

## Forging minigame

- You get 3 hammer strikes in total. Strike with Space or a click.
- A marker slides back and forth, and the closer to the center you hit, the higher your score. The marker moves faster for higher-tier materials, and speeds up by 1.12x with each strike.
- Scoring: within 0.03 of center is 1.0 (perfect), within 0.07 is 0.7, within 0.13 is 0.4, and anything else is 0.1.
- An average of 0.95 or higher across the three strikes gives ★3, 0.65 or higher gives ★2, and anything below gives ★1.

## Defense

Base defense per piece: helmet 2, chestplate 4, leggings 3, boots 1.5

- Material multipliers: Leather 0.8, Iron 1, Copper 1.2, Reinforced Iron 1.45, Gold 2.1, Reinforced Copper 1.75, Reinforced Gold 2.5, Crystal 2.9, Obsidian 3.3, Frost 3.1
- Quality multipliers: ★1 is 0.85, ★2 is 1.0, ★3 is 1.2
- Damage reduction = total defense / (total defense + 25). An Ironskin Potion multiplies this by an extra x0.8.

## Full-set defense and damage reduction (★1 / ★2 / ★3)

- Leather: 7.1 (22%) / 8.4 (25%) / 10.1 (29%)
- Iron: 8.9 (26%) / 10.5 (30%) / 12.6 (34%)
- Copper: 10.7 (30%) / 12.6 (34%) / 15.1 (38%)
- Reinforced Iron: 12.9 (34%) / 15.2 (38%) / 18.3 (42%)
- Reinforced Copper: 15.6 (38%) / 18.4 (42%) / 22.1 (47%)
- Gold: 18.7 (43%) / 22.1 (47%) / 26.5 (51%)
- Reinforced Gold: 22.3 (47%) / 26.2 (51%) / 31.5 (56%)
- Crystal: 25.9 (51%) / 30.4 (55%) / 36.5 (59%)
- Frost: 27.7 (53%) / 32.6 (57%) / 39.1 (61%)
- Obsidian: 29.5 (54%) / 34.6 (58%) / 41.6 (62%)

## Equipping and durability

- Hold a piece of armor and **right-click** to equip it.
- Armor durability = material base durability x piece multiplier (helmet 1, chestplate 1.4, leggings 1.2, boots 0.8) x quality multiplier (★1 0.8, ★2 1, ★3 1.25).
- Every time you get hit, every armor piece you're wearing loses 1 durability, and it breaks at 0.
- You can repair it with a hammer at an Anvil. This uses up the hammer's durability.

## Terrain protection

- Full leather set: Blocks the cold on Ice Islands.
- Full obsidian set or a Fire Resistance Potion: Blocks lava, the heat of Volcanic Islands and burns from spreading fire. While protected, standing on lava produces one volcanic rock every 1.5 seconds.

## Recommendations

- Early on, a full leather or iron set is plenty.
- If you're heading to Ice Islands, it's handy to keep a separate leather set.
- Higher tiers need island materials like crystal and frost shards. Give them a go later on.

beaconfall/potions-runes.b:
:: Potion brewing = Cauldron
:: Potions per brew = 2
:: Duration = 300–480 seconds
:: Throw range = 110
:: Rune Altar = 4 stone + 1 crystal
:: Runes = Fire, Frost, Venom, Life

Brew potions in the **Cauldron** and engrave elements onto weapons at the **Rune Altar**.

## Cauldron

- The Cauldron is made at the Workbench from 2 iron ingots, 2 clay and 1 branch.
- Mixing ingredients gives you **2** potions. A wrong combination gives just 1 ash, and the ingredients are lost.

## Potion recipes and effects

- **Healing**: Leaves + slime. HP +10
- **Swiftness**: Feather + 2 leaves. Move speed +15%, 300 seconds
- **Strength**: Raw meat + bone + ash. Attack x1.25, 300 seconds
- **Ironskin**: Clay + leather. Damage taken x0.8, 300 seconds
- **Night Vision**: Crystal + slime. Better vision at night, 480 seconds
- **Breathing**: Frost shard + mangrove root. Extends oxygen at reefs, 480 seconds

There are also terrain potions (sold by the village sailor).

- **Fire Resistance Potion**: Protects from lava, Volcanic Island heat and burns from spreading fire, 300 seconds
- **Antidote**: Protects from poison in jungles and mangroves, 300 seconds
- **Cactus Juice**: Protects from heat in deserts and mesas, 300 seconds

## Throwing

Hold a potion and press Ctrl to throw it. Radius 26, range 110.

- Allies get the same buff.
- On monsters: Swiftness slows for 6 seconds, Strength deals 4 damage, Ironskin stuns for 2 seconds, Night Vision slows for 4 seconds and stuns for 1.2 seconds, and Breathing deals damage over time.

## Buff types

- spd: Movement x1.15
- atk: Attack x1.25
- def: Damage taken x0.8
- work: Work time x0.78
- reg: HP +1 every 8 seconds
- night, breath: Night Vision and Breathing

## Rune Altar

- The Rune Altar is made from 4 stone and 1 crystal.
- Rune materials (1 crystal each, plus the following):
- **Fire**: 2 ash. Damage +30%, plus 0.7 burn damage per second for 3.2 seconds. If there is something flammable where it hits, there is a 35% chance it catches fire, and monsters set ablaze spread fire where they walk (spreading fire)
- **Frost**: 2 frost shards. Slows for 3.5 seconds
- **Venom**: 2 snake fangs. 0.5 poison damage per second for about 5 seconds
- **Life**: 2 leaves + 1 slime. Heals 1 HP per hit, 1.2-second cooldown
- Runes work on longswords, daggers and axes. A new rune overwrites the old one.

## Another use for ash

Hold ash and right-click near crops to cut their remaining growth time to 35%.

## Tips

- Drink Strength and Ironskin together right before a boss fight. They last 300 seconds, enough for about one dungeon level.
- Bring a full leather set for Ice Island trips and Cactus Juice for deserts and mesas to save HP.
- Night Vision Potions brighten up your view at night.

## How to use runes

1. Place a Rune Altar (4 stone, 1 crystal).
2. Hold your weapon and interact with the altar.
3. Prepare the rune materials (1 crystal plus the rune's specific materials).
4. Engraving earns you the Rune Engraving achievement.

## Potion achievements

- First Alchemy: When you brew your first potion in the Cauldron
- Grand Alchemist: When you discover every combination
- Grenadier: When you throw a potion for the first time

beaconfall/food-cooking.b:
:: Where to cook = Campfire, Hearth
:: Gourmet dishes = Needs a Cooking Pot
:: Required book = Gourmet Cookbook
:: Best healing = HP +8
:: Full Course = All 4 buffs, 360 seconds
:: Book price = 90 coins

Food restores HP and gives buffs. You can only eat when your HP isn't full or there's a buff to apply. Eat with right-click. Raw meat can't be eaten; you have to cook it.

## Where to cook

- Within 26 pixels of the starting camp's **Campfire**, or at a **Hearth** (6 stone)
- Gourmet dishes need a **Cooking Pot** (3 iron or copper ingots + 1 branch), and you have to buy the Gourmet Cookbook (90 coins).

## Basic dishes

- **Bread**: 3 wheat. HP +3, movement buff for 180 seconds
- **Baked Potato**: 1 potato. HP +2, work buff for 180 seconds
- **Popcorn**: 1 corn. HP +1, movement buff for 90 seconds
- **Fried Egg**: 1 egg. HP +2, defense buff for 180 seconds
- **Milk**: HP +2, regeneration for 60 seconds
- **Cooked Meat**: 1 raw meat. HP +5, attack buff for 240 seconds
- **Stew**: 2 potatoes + 1 corn + 1 milk. HP +6, regeneration for 240 seconds and defense for 120 seconds
- **Grilled Fish**: Any fish except legendary (common to rare). HP +4, attack for 180 seconds
- Raw fish gives HP +1.

## Gourmet dishes (Cooking Pot)

- **Seafood Soup**: 2 fish (common to rare) + potato + corn. HP +7, attack and movement for 240 seconds
- **Full Course**: Cooked Meat + Bread + Fried Egg + Baked Potato. HP +8, all 4 buffs for 360 seconds
- **Marlin Dish**: Marlin + potato + corn. HP +8, attack and movement for 420 seconds
- **Golden Carp Dish**: Golden carp + potato + corn. HP +8, defense, regeneration and work for 420 seconds

## Buff summary

- Move speed x1.15
- Attack x1.25
- Damage taken x0.8
- Work time x0.78
- HP +1 every 8 seconds

## Getting food

- Chickens drop 1 raw meat, feathers (60%) and leather (50%)
- Cows drop 2–3 raw meat and 1–2 leather
- Birds drop 1–2 feathers, with a 40% chance of raw meat
- Chickens and cows can be tamed for eggs and milk. See the Farming & Animals page.
- Wheat, potatoes and corn are grown in fields.

## Tips

- The Full Course is the most solid meal before a dungeon. It takes a lot of ingredients, but you get every buff at once.
- Fish a lot and you'll unlock Seafood Soup and the legendary fish dishes.
- Stew only needs field crops and a cow, so it's a great starter dish.

## How to eat

- Hold food and right-click to eat it.
- If your HP is full and there's no new buff to give, you can't eat it.

## Recommended meals

- Early game: Cooked Meat (HP +5, attack for 240 seconds)
- Mid game: Stew (HP +6, regeneration and defense)
- Late game: Full Course (HP +8, all buffs for 360 seconds)
- On a good fishing day: Seafood Soup (HP +7, attack and movement for 240 seconds)

## Getting ingredients

- 3 wheat makes one loaf of bread. Wheat grows in the field in 50–70 seconds.
- Once you tame a cow, you get milk every 100 seconds.
- Chickens lay eggs after eating seeds.

beaconfall/farming-animals.b:
:: Wheat growth = 50–70 seconds
:: Potato growth = 70–90 seconds
:: Corn growth = 90–120 seconds
:: Rain = Crops grow 2x faster
:: Tamed animal cap = 24
:: Trap = 1 animal every 90 seconds

Fields and livestock give you a steady source of food and coins.

## Farming

1. Till the soil with a **hoe**. Each tile uses 1 durability.
2. Plant seeds. Wheat seeds are made at the Workbench from 1 wheat. You can also buy seeds at Mina the farmer's shop in the village.
3. Wait for them to grow, then harvest when they're fully grown.

- Wheat: grows in 50–70 seconds, harvest 2
- Potato: grows in 70–90 seconds, harvest 2–4
- Corn: grows in 90–120 seconds, harvest 2–3
- When it rains, crops grow 2x faster and saplings 1.5x faster.
- Hold ash and right-click a growing crop to cut its remaining time to 35%.

## Saplings

- Saplings take 20–45 seconds to become trees. Planting on tilled soil makes it 10 seconds faster.
- You can also buy saplings at village shops.

## Weather and seasons

- Weather changes between clear, rain and storms. At night you hear waves and crickets, and rain and storms bring the sound of rain.
- In storms, lightning can start fires. Crops and saplings in your fields burn too, so it helps to keep a bucket filled with water. When it rains, fire spreads poorly.
- Seasons change every 7 days and are shown on the clock. We haven't confirmed whether seasons have any other gameplay effects.

## Animals

- **Chicken**: 3 HP. After eating seeds (wheat seeds, potatoes, corn), it lays an egg 15–25 seconds later.
- **Cow**: 8 HP. Feed it wheat, potatoes or corn and it gives milk every 100 seconds.
- **Bird**: 2 HP. Drops feathers when caught.
- You can have up to 24 tamed animals.
- Fed pairs breed (40 seconds of love), and babies grow up after 90 seconds.
- When killed: cows drop 2–3 raw meat and 1–2 leather, chickens drop 1 raw meat plus feathers 60% and leather 50%, and birds drop 1–2 feathers and raw meat 40%.

## Traps

- Traps are made from 3 branches, 2 string and 1 plank.
- For bait, put in up to 5 of raw meat, wheat, potatoes, corn or eggs.
- One animal is caught every 90 seconds, and it holds up to 24.
- By default you get raw meat, leather and feathers, plus local items depending on the island, like eggs, feathers, snake fangs, bones and frost shards.

## Aquarium

Made from 3 planks and 3 slime. Put the fish you catch in it and watch them swim.

## Horses and carts

You can buy a horse (500 coins, Neighbor rank or higher) and a cart (250 coins, Resident rank or higher) from the village farmer. See the Transportation page.

## Tips

- There's a 24-animal limit on tamed livestock, so don't let your herd grow too big.
- Rainy days are great for saving time in the fields.
- Selling crops with high village prices at the market also raises prosperity.

## Field management tips

- Better hoe materials have more durability, so the 1-per-tile cost hurts less.
- Plant all three crops to earn the Farmer achievement.
- Tame livestock by feeding them to earn the Rancher achievement.
- Ash only works on crops that are still growing.

beaconfall/fishing.b:
:: Tiers = 4 (Common to Legendary)
:: Legendary fish = Marlin, Golden Carp
:: Minigame = 30-second limit
:: Sell price = 4, 10, 24, 60 coins
:: Best rod = Reinforced Gold (power 7)
:: Tournament fee = 20 coins

Fishing is a laid-back activity that leads to food, coins and even legendary fish dishes.

## How to fish

1. Hold a fishing rod and click near water to cast.
2. When you get a bite, click again to start the minigame.
3. Use the A and D keys to follow the moving zone and keep the marker inside it. The time limit is 30 seconds.
4. If you fail, you'll see "It got away."

## Fish tiers

There are four tiers: Common, Uncommon, Rare and Legendary.

- Sea: Anchovy (Common), Mackerel (Common), Sea Bream (Uncommon), Flounder (Uncommon), Tuna (Rare), Pufferfish (Rare), **Marlin** (Legendary)
- River: Crucian Carp (Common), Minnow (Common), Trout (Uncommon), Catfish (Uncommon), Carp (Rare), Sturgeon (Rare), **Golden Carp** (Legendary)
- Some of the fish you can catch differ by island.

Older pages listed Marlin and Golden Carp as Rare, but they're actually **Legendary**.

## Fishing rods and odds

- Rod power by material: Log 1, Stone 1.2, Reinforced Wood 1.5, Iron 2, Copper 2.5, Reinforced Iron 3.2, Gold 4.3, Reinforced Copper 4, Reinforced Gold 7
- Tier weights are 70/p to the power of 0.35, 22 x p to the power of 0.4, 7 x p to the power of 0.9, and p to the power of 1.5 (where p is power). The higher the power, the more Rare and Legendary catches.
- When a Rare is rolled, there's a 30% chance you get a metal item instead (gold ingot, Reinforced Copper, Reinforced Iron, gold axe).

## Selling prices

Fish sell for a base of 4, 10, 24 and 60 coins by tier. Kuro the wandering merchant buys fish at 1.5x.

## Fishing tournament

- Enter once a day through Haru the sailor in the village. The entry fee is 20 coins, and the time limit is 180 seconds.
- Prizes by rank: 1st 150 coins + 3 crystal, 2nd 90 coins + 2 gold ingots, 3rd 50 coins, 4th 30 coins, 5th 15 coins
- Winning earns the "Fishing Tournament Champion" achievement.

## Uses

- Grilled Fish (any non-legendary fish) is an easy attack-buff food.
- Seafood Soup and the legendary fish dishes need a Cooking Pot. See the cooking page.
- Aiming for the Fish Encyclopedia and Legendary Angler achievements is a fun goal too.
- Fishing rods have a x0.7 durability multiplier, so metal ones last longer.

## Bite and minigame tips

- It takes two clicks: one to cast, one to react to the bite.
- In the minigame, use A and D to keep the marker in the zone. You have to finish within 30 seconds.
- Metal rods raise your Legendary odds, so the Reinforced Gold rod (power 7) is the best.
- If you're after Rare or better, upgrade your rod first.

## What you get from fishing

- Common fish become HP +4 attack-buff food when grilled.
- Rare fish sell for 24 coins. Legendaries sell for 60 coins and are worth even more as cooking ingredients.
- The Marlin Dish and Golden Carp Dish need a Cooking Pot and the Gourmet Cookbook.
- You can also put them in an aquarium to watch.

## Achievements

- Legendary Angler (catch a legendary), Fish Encyclopedia (every fish), Fishing Tournament Champion (1st place)

beaconfall/islands-dungeon-bosses.b:
:: Islands = 30
:: Island bosses = 8
:: Boss respawn = 2 days later
:: Enrage = Below half HP
:: Dungeon = 5 levels (+ undersea level)
:: No-boss islands = Village and Pirate Islands

The world of BEACONFALL is made up of 30 islands scattered across the sea. This page gives you the big picture; details are on the Island Types & Hazards, Boss Guide, Monster Guide and Dungeon pages.

## Island lineup

- 1 Starting Island
- 4 Forest Islands, 4 Desert Islands, 4 Jungle Islands, 4 Mangrove Islands, 4 Ice Islands
- 3 Volcanic Islands, 3 Mesa Islands, 3 Stone Islands
- That's 30 in total. A code comment somewhere says 28, but that's an outdated number; 30 are actually generated.
- **Village Island**: One of the Forest Islands becomes the village. It's a safe island with no monsters.
- **Pirate Island**: The island farthest from the start (excluding Volcanic and Village Islands) becomes the Pirate Island. Pirates spawn there.
- Village and Pirate Islands have no bosses.
- **Ruined Island**: one large island gets a collapsed old palace and a ruined village. See the Island Types & Hazards page.

## Eight bosses, one per island type

- Forest Island: Wolf King
- Desert Island: Giant Scorpion
- Volcanic Island: Fire Giant
- Jungle Island: Venom Spider Queen
- Mesa Island: Sand Serpent
- Stone Island: Rock Giant
- Mangrove Island: Swamp Croc King
- Ice Island: Great Yeti

A boss appears when you get within about 55% of the island's radius from its center. After you defeat it, it comes back 2 days later. Below half HP, it enrages, gaining more patterns and chasing 1.25x faster. Every pattern shows a warning (wind-up) before the attack.

Each of the eight bosses drops its own relic every time it's defeated. Collect all 8 relics to craft the Void Core and you can challenge the final boss, the Void Lord (Void Lord & True Ending page).

## Recommended exploration order

1. Get iron gear on the Starting Island.
2. Build a boat (5 planks + 2 iron ingots).
3. Head to the Forest Island with the village and buy books and consumables.
4. Start with low-hazard islands like Forest, Mesa and Stone Islands.
5. For Desert, Jungle, Mangrove, Ice and Volcanic Islands, prepare the matching potions or armor before you go.

## Map and Journal

- Hold a map item (Island Map) and press Ctrl to open the map. Places you've visited are cleared of fog, and with a map item, every island marker shows up. Islands you haven't visited yet are yellow.
- The map also shows graves, merchant ships, wandering markets and treasure chests you've seen.
- The Journal (V) collects island stamps. There are rewards based on how many islands you've discovered: 5 islands 60 coins, 10 islands 3 crystal + 120 coins, 20 islands 4 gold ingots + 300 coins, all of them 5 crystal + 600 coins

## Dungeon

There's a 5-level underground dungeon you enter through a cave entrance near the Starting Island, plus a 6th undersea level if there's room. See the Dungeon page for details.

## Reefs and sky

- At whirlpools (reefs) in the sea, you can go diving with Diving Gear.
- With a hot air balloon, you can find cloud treasure above the islands.
- With a hot air balloon you can also enter the sky fortress. The Sky Guardian waits in its throne room. See the Sky Fortress page.
- Ghost ships appear on the sea at night. See the Transportation page.

## Signature materials by island

- Forest Island: Resin, bones, maple
- Desert Island: Cactus fiber
- Volcanic Island: Volcanic rock, ash
- Jungle Island: Rubber
- Mesa Island: Clay, copper
- Stone Island: Crystal, zinc, ore
- Mangrove Island: Mangrove roots, leather
- Ice Island: Frost shards, iron, copper

## Progression tips

- Reefs and sky treasure are great sources of coins and rare materials.
- The first chest at the ruins is on top of the altar.
- Every new island you discover adds a stamp to your Journal.

beaconfall/island-types.b:
:: Island types = Starting Island + 8
:: Desert & Mesa = Daytime heat, Cactus Juice
:: Jungle & Mangrove = Poison, Antidote
:: Volcanic Island = Lava and heat, Fire Resistance
:: Ice Island = Cold, full leather set
:: Stone Island = Falling rocks (1.2 s warning)
:: Ruined Island = 1 large island (old palace, ruined village)
:: Spreading fire = Lightning, fire rune, lava; put out with a bucket

Each island has its own hazards and monsters. Packing the right countermeasures makes life a lot easier.

The Islands tab of the site compendium shows each island's tree ratios, ore ratios among rocks, special drops, monsters and boss.

## Starting Island

- Low danger. Slimes come out at night.
- Trees are a mix of pine, shrubs, oak, zelkova and maple.
- Rocks are only found in the highlands.
- The ruins are the wreckage of your crashed ship. The dungeon entrance is near the Starting Island too.

## Forest Islands (4)

- No environmental hazards. At night, it's 70% wolves and 30% slimes, and wolves also show up during the day 35% of the time.
- 55% pine, 35% oak and zelkova, 10% maple
- The village spawns on one of the Forest Islands. The boss is the **Wolf King**.
- Ruins: Pillar garden

## Desert Islands (4)

- Hazard: During the day (7 AM–7 PM), 0.5 damage every 5 seconds. Block it with **Cactus Juice** (300 seconds).
- Monsters: Scorpions. Trees are 70% cactus, so cactus fiber is plentiful.
- Boss: Giant Scorpion. Ruins: Step pyramid
- Desert and Mesa Islands have giant whale-bone fossils.

## Volcanic Islands (3)

- Hazard: Lava deals 1 damage plus burning every 0.5 seconds. Heat deals 0.5 damage every 6 seconds. Block it with a **Fire Resistance Potion** (300 seconds) or a full obsidian set. Burning deals 1 damage per second.
- Monsters: Fire Spirits (burning). Trees are 80% dead trees.
- There's a real volcano and lava, plus crater fire ring ruins.
- The volcano erupts periodically. A rumble comes first, then a column of ash and lava bombs shoot up. It's just for show and deals no damage.
- Trees near lava sometimes catch fire and it spreads (see Spreading fire below).
- Boss: Fire Giant. You can get volcanic rock here.

## Jungle Islands (4)

- Hazard: Every 10 seconds, poison for 4 seconds (0.5 per second). Block it with an **Antidote** (300 seconds).
- Monsters: Spiders (poison). Trees are 60% palm, which drop rubber.
- Boss: Venom Spider Queen. Ruins: Mossy temple

## Mesa Islands (3)

- Hazard: Daytime heat damage, same as the desert. You'll need Cactus Juice. (This wasn't in the older pages.)
- Monsters: Snakes. Rocks have a 70% chance of dropping clay. Rich in copper.
- Boss: Sand Serpent. Ruins: Arch pillars

## Stone Islands (3)

- Hazard: Rocks fall every 6–11 seconds. After a 1.2-second warning, they deal 2 damage.
- Monsters: Golems. Rocks have a 35% chance of dropping crystal. The richest in zinc and every ore.
- Boss: Rock Giant. Ruins: Cross-shaped megalith

## Mangrove Islands (4)

- Hazard: Poison, like the jungle. You'll need an **Antidote**. Move speed is slowed to x0.8.
- Monsters: Crocodiles. Mangrove trees drop mangrove roots (an ingredient for Breathing Potions).
- Boss: Swamp Croc King. Ruins: Stilt-house site

## Ice Islands (4)

- Hazard: Cold deals 0.5 damage every 5 seconds (every 3 seconds at night). Wearing a **full leather set** blocks it.
- Monsters: Yetis. Rocks have a 50% chance of dropping frost shards. Rich in iron and copper.
- Boss: Great Yeti. Ruins: Fortress

## Village and Pirate Islands

- The Village Island is safe, with NPCs, trading and cottages.
- Pirates spawn on the Pirate Island (18 HP, 3 damage). Plundering them gives arrows, iron ingots and planks.

## Ruined Island
- One large island gets a collapsed old palace and a ruined village. The island is named Ruined Island.
- The starting, village, pirate and volcanic islands are not chosen. It is picked from the large islands that have room for both the palace and the village, and islands without a grand temple come first.
- **Old palace**: it has crumbled walls and a gate, a courtyard with standing pillars (some have fallen) and a throne room.
- There are **4 treasure chests** in and around the throne room. They are filled only once per world, with 80–199 coins and 4–6 kinds of valuable items.
- **Ruined village**: roofless, crumbled houses, a well and weeds.
- It is decorated with vines and moss, low-lying mist, tattered banners, fallen pillars, broken statues and piles of leaves.

## Grand temple ruins and lighthouses
- Grand temple ruins appear on 3 large islands, with rows of tall pillars, giant statues, an altar and treasure chests. They also appear in worlds you already made when you open them again.
- The coasts have up to 4 lighthouses, with crates and barrels on their docks. At night the lighthouse beam sweeps across the sea.

## Scenery
- At sea, the shadows of giant whales pass by and their spouts shoot up.
- You'll see mist at dawn, a red sunset with a low sun at dusk, light shafts at midday and shooting stars at night.
- In storms, lightning bolts strike and the screen shakes.
- On winter nights the aurora shows even away from the Ice Islands.
- Whales are easier to see when they surface, and the aurora and shooting stars are brighter than before.
- Ruin walls carry paintings of the sun, waves, trees, flames, stars and snow. The runes on pillars and giant statues glow brighter at night, and a ring of runes turns around the altars.
- Trees change color with the seasons: blossoming trees in spring, autumn leaves in fall and snow-covered trees in winter, and village roofs get winter snow, autumn leaves and spring petals too.
- Volcano rock and lava no longer have square borders and blend naturally into neighboring tiles. The outer edges are rugged and the lava pools are rounder.
- The screen design has been polished. The top buttons now share a wood-and-brass look, the selected tile has a golden breathing effect, the heart bar has a base, and window titles have decorative lines.

## Spreading fire

- Added in build 84. When forests or wooden structures catch fire, the fire spreads to neighboring tiles.
- There are three causes. During storms, lightning strikes trees or wooden structures near players; monsters set ablaze by a fire rune weapon spread fire where they walk; and trees near volcanic lava catch fire.
- Fire burns for 6–12 seconds on a tile and spreads to neighboring trees and wooden structures meanwhile. When it burns out, trees, saplings, crops and wooden buildings and furniture (Workbench, Storage Box, Bed, fence, door, wooden wall, roof, table, chair, bookshelf, Villager House, etc.) are gone. Burnt trees sometimes leave ash, and burnt structures drop only what was inside them, without their materials.
- In rain or storms, fire spreads poorly and burning fires sometimes go out.
- Touching fire gives you burning (1 damage per second). If you have drunk a Fire Resistance Potion or are wearing a full obsidian (volcanic rock) set, you don't get burned.
- Hold a **Bucket** (4 planks + 1 branch, crafted by hand) and right-click by water or a well to fill it, turning it into a Water Bucket. Hold the Water Bucket and right-click next to a fire to put out the nearest fire and the fire around it; it turns back into an empty bucket you can use again.

## General hazards

- **Elite monsters**: Appear 12% of the time (30% during raids), have 2.5x HP and drop 1–2 gold ingots.
- **Night Raids**: Happen at about a 0.008% chance per second per player and spawn 8 monsters nearby.
- Monster spawning: Up to about 2 + player count at once (capped at 5–6), one every 8–14 seconds. Slimes disappear during the day, but other monsters stay.

## Gear checklist

- Desert and Mesa: Cactus Juice
- Jungle and Mangrove: Antidote
- Volcanic: Fire Resistance Potion or a full obsidian set
- Ice: Full leather set
- Stone: Watch for falling rock warnings
- Spreading fire: A bucket filled with water

beaconfall/monsters.b:
:: Elite chance = 12% (30% during raids)
:: Elite HP = 2.5x
:: Highest HP = Ghost Ship (110)
:: Toughest boss = Rock Giant (150 HP)
:: Status effects = Poison, burning
:: Max at once = 5–6

Here are the HP, damage and drops of every monster. In the dungeon, HP goes up depending on the level.

## Regular monsters

- **Slime**: 8 HP, 2 damage. 1–2 slime. Appears at night on the Starting Island and Forest Islands. Disappears during the day.
- **Wolf**: 10 HP, 2 damage. 1–2 bones. Forest Islands.
- **Scorpion**: 9 HP, 2 damage, poison. 0–1 cactus fiber. Desert Islands.
- **Fire Spirit**: 10 HP, 3 damage, burning. 1–2 volcanic rock or 0–1 ash. Volcanic Islands.
- **Spider**: 8 HP, 1.5 damage, poison. 1–2 string. Jungle Islands.
- **Snake**: 7 HP, 2 damage. 1 snake fang. Mesa Islands.
- **Golem**: 24 HP, 4 damage. One of stone, iron or copper. Stone Islands.
- **Crocodile**: 16 HP, 3 damage. 1–2 leather. Mangrove Islands.
- **Yeti**: 14 HP, 3 damage. 0–1 frost shard or bone. Ice Islands.
- **Pirate**: 18 HP, 3 damage. 0–3 arrows, 0–1 iron ingot, 0–2 planks. Pirate Island.
- **Ghost Ship**: 110 HP, 2.5 damage. 2–3 crystal, 2–4 gold ingots, 1–3 pearls, plus the treasure table. Appears on the night sea with a 55% chance each day.

Scorpions, spiders and their bosses inflict poison, while Fire Spirits and the Fire Giant inflict burning.

## Elite monsters

- Appear 12% of the time, 30% during raids.
- They have 2.5x HP, drop 1–2 gold ingots, and sometimes extra treasure.

## Boss summary (details on the Boss Guide page)

- Wolf King: 70 HP, 3 damage
- Giant Scorpion: 80 HP, 3 damage
- Fire Giant: 140 HP, 3.5 damage
- Venom Spider Queen: 90 HP, 2.5 damage
- Sand Serpent: 80 HP, 3 damage
- Rock Giant: 150 HP, 4 damage
- Swamp Croc King: 100 HP, 4 damage
- Great Yeti: 120 HP, 4 damage

## Animals

Chickens, cows and birds are animals, not monsters. See the Farming & Animals page.

## How to deal with them

- Drink an Antidote first against poisonous monsters.
- Against burning monsters, a Fire Resistance Potion or obsidian armor works well.
- Golems have high HP and damage, so fight them at range with a bow or use an Ironskin Potion.
- Boost your attack with meat buffs (eat with right-click).
- Runes: Frost slows and Fire burns, which makes them handy against fleeing monsters.

## Achievements

Defeating monsters advances the Monster Encyclopedia and other combat achievements. See the Achievements page.

## Spawn rules

- The only night-only monsters are slimes on the Starting Island and Forest Islands. They disappear during the day.
- Wolves on Forest Islands can appear during the day too (35% by day, 70% at night).
- Deserts have scorpions, volcanoes have Fire Spirits, jungles have spiders, mesas have snakes, Stone Islands have golems, mangroves have crocodiles, and ice has yetis.
- No monsters spawn on the Village Island.
- The number of monsters at once is close to 2 + player count, capped at 5–6.

## Raids

- Night Raids happen at a low chance per player, and when one hits, 8 monsters spawn nearby.
- During a raid, the elite chance goes up from 12% to 30%.

beaconfall/bosses.b:
:: Island bosses = 8
:: HP range = 70–150
:: Highest HP = Rock Giant (150)
:: Enrage = At 50% HP or below
:: Respawn = 2 days later
:: Recommended rune = Fire (+30% damage)
:: Final boss = Void Lord (700 HP)

Every boss follows the same rules. A warning (wind-up) appears before each pattern. When a boss enrages at 50% HP or below, new patterns unlock, its chase speed goes up x1.25 and the gaps between patterns get shorter. Patterns marked with an asterisk below only appear while enraged.

## Common rules

- Bosses appear when you get within about 55% of the island's radius from its center.
- After you defeat one, it comes back 2 days later.
- Rewards include 3–5 rolls on the treasure table on top of the boss's own drops.
- Each time you defeat an island boss, it drops its own relic (8 kinds, such as the Wolf King's Relic and the Scorpion's Relic). Relics are the materials for summoning the Void Lord; the dungeon level 5 boss gives no relic.

## Pattern glossary

- **Dash** (dash): 0.75-second warning, length 140. The long dash (dashL) is 0.9 seconds and 230, and the short dash (dashS) is 0.6 seconds and 110.
- **Slam** (slam): Radius 38, empowered version (slamB) 54
- **Leap** (leap): Radius 32, empowered version 48
- **Shockwave** (ring): An expanding ring
- **Falling attack** (rain): Attacks that drop from above. From smallest: rainS 3, rain 5, rainM 7, and boulders 9 projectiles.
- **Ice spikes** (lane): 7 spikes erupt one after another.
- **Summon** (summon): 3 wolves, 3 spiders or 2 crocodiles. Up to 6 summons at once, +1 when enraged.
- **Burrow** (burrow): Erupts in a radius of 30 after 1.9 seconds.
- **Cone** (cone): Radius 50
- **Beam** (beam): Length 210
- **Zones** (zones): Poison, fire or earth patches that last 7 seconds and deal 0.45x damage every 0.6 seconds.
- **Aura** (aura): 4 seconds, radius 64

## Wolf King (Forest Island)

- 70 HP, 3 damage. Drops: 3–5 bones, 3–5 resin
- Patterns: Dash, wolf summon, cone, long dash when enraged
- Strategy: The dash warning is short, so sidestep it. Take out the summoned wolves first.

## Giant Scorpion (Desert Island)

- 80 HP, 3 damage. Drops: 5–8 cactus fiber
- Patterns: Burrow, cone, small falling attack, zones when enraged
- Strategy: It poisons, so bring both an Antidote and Cactus Juice.

## Fire Giant (Volcanic Island)

- 140 HP, 3.5 damage. Drops: 4–6 volcanic rock, 4–6 ash
- Patterns: Shockwave, medium falling attack, empowered slam, zones when enraged
- Strategy: With burning and heat, a Fire Resistance Potion is practically a must.

## Venom Spider Queen (Jungle Island)

- 90 HP, 2.5 damage. Drops: 4–6 rubber
- Patterns: Beam, spider summon, leap, zones when enraged
- Strategy: Watch the beam's direction and move to the side. You'll need an Antidote.

## Sand Serpent (Mesa Island)

- 80 HP, 3 damage. Drops: 6–9 clay
- Patterns: Long dash, slam, beam, burrow when enraged
- Strategy: The long dash covers 230, so dodge far away right from the start.

## Rock Giant (Stone Island)

- 150 HP, 4 damage. Drops: 4–6 crystal, 6–10 stone
- Patterns: Empowered leap, falling boulders, shockwave, empowered slam when enraged
- Strategy: It has the most HP. An Ironskin Potion and good armor help.

## Swamp Croc King (Mangrove Island)

- 100 HP, 4 damage. Drops: 3–5 leather, 4–6 mangrove roots
- Patterns: Short dash, slam, zones, crocodile summon, leap when enraged
- Strategy: Short dashes and slams come often. Keep your distance.

## Great Yeti (Ice Island)

- 120 HP, 4 damage. Drops: 5–8 frost shards, 3–5 bones
- Patterns: Aura, ice spikes, leap, shockwave when enraged
- Strategy: The aura is wide, with a radius of 64. You'll need a full leather set because of the cold.

## Ghost Ship (night sea)

- 110 HP, 2.5 damage. Patterns: Shockwave, medium falling attack, falling attack, falling boulders when enraged
- Rewards are 2–3 crystal, 2–4 gold ingots, 1–3 pearls and the treasure table.

## Sky Guardian (sky fortress)
- 299 HP (1.15 times the base 260), 4.5 damage. It appears only in the throne room of the sky fortress, and looks like a winged armored knight.
- Patterns: Ice spikes, shockwave, empowered leap, medium falling attack, beam, zones and falling boulders when enraged
- Rewards: 5–7 crystal, 5–7 gold ingots and 2 pearls, plus its usual drop (2–3 crystal) and the treasure table.
- After you defeat it, it returns 3 days later. That differs from the 2 days of island bosses.
- Defeating it for the first time earns the Lord of the Sky achievement. See the Sky Fortress page for details.

## Dungeon level 5 boss

See the Dungeon page. It's one of the Rock Giant, Fire Giant, Great Yeti or Venom Spider Queen, decided by the seed.

## Void Lord (final boss)
- It appears when you use the Void Core made from the 8 relics at night and survive the ritual. It has 700 HP and 5.5 attack, and at 75, 50 and 25% HP it raises a barrier and calls 4 minions. See the Void Lord & True Ending page for the full guide.

## Tips

- Before a boss fight, bring Strength, Ironskin and a Full Course.
- Restore your durability at an Anvil before taking on a boss.
- Among runes, Fire raises damage by 30%, which is great for boss fights.

beaconfall/dungeon.b:
:: Levels = 5 (+ undersea level)
:: Level size = 40x40 tiles
:: Rooms = Up to 9 per level
:: Level 5 boss = 1 of 4, set by seed
:: Level reset = Every 3 days
:: Party revive = Within 45 seconds

The dungeon has 5 levels (plus a 6th undersea level if there's room). Each level is 40x40 tiles with up to 9 rooms, and has stairs going up and down.

## Entrance

- The dungeon cave entrance is on the island closest to the start (usually the Starting Island), away from the camp. We haven't confirmed whether it's always the Starting Island.

## Monsters by level

1. Level 1: Spiders, snakes
2. Level 2: Spiders, snakes, wolves
3. Level 3: Wolves, golems, scorpions
4. Level 4: Golems, Fire Spirits, yetis
5. Level 5: Golems, Fire Spirits, crocodiles, yetis

- Monster HP is 1 + 0.22 x (level - 1) times normal.
- The elite chance is 10% + 5% x level, with 2.5x HP.

## Chests

- 3 chests in the last room (5 on level 5)
- Other rooms have a 75% chance of 1
- Contents are ore, materials and coins (8 + 10 x level + 0–19).

## Level resets

If nobody is on a level, it's regenerated every 3 days.

## Level 5 boss

- One of the Rock Giant, Fire Giant, Great Yeti or Venom Spider Queen, decided by the seed.
- It has 1.15x HP.
- After you defeat it, it comes back 3 days later.
- Rewards: 3–4 crystal, 3–5 gold ingots, treasure table (once per player present, up to 3 times)

## Party revive

In the dungeon, a downed player can be revived by a teammate within 45 seconds. They come back with half HP. If no teammate is on the same level, it's a normal death.

## Reef diving

- Take a boat near a whirlpool and press F to dive. You need **Diving Gear**.
- Oxygen lasts 60 seconds, or 150 seconds with a Breathing Potion. If you run out of oxygen, you take 3 damage and surface.
- Reef chests contain coral, pearls, crystal, gold ingots, Breathing Potions, rubber and 30–69 coins.
- There's an undersea exploration achievement.

## Preparation

- Healing Potions, Full Course, Ironskin, Strength
- Iron-tier or better gear and armor
- A good bow and a few dozen arrows

## Level layout in detail

- Each level is 40x40 tiles with up to 9 rooms, plus stairs going up and stairs going down.
- The 6th undersea level only appears if there's room.
- Monsters on each level come from the list above. Golems show up from level 3, so bring Ironskin Potions.

## Clearing order

1. Levels 1 and 2 have spiders and snakes, so prepare for poison (Antidotes) before going in.
2. Level 3 mixes wolves, golems and scorpions. Keep your distance with a bow.
3. Levels 4 and 5 have Fire Spirits (burning) and yetis. Bring Fire Resistance Potions.
4. The last room on level 5 has 5 chests and the boss.

## Elite chance breakdown

- Level 1 15%, level 2 20%, level 3 25%, level 4 30%, level 5 35% (10% + 5% x level)
- Elites have 2.5x normal HP and drop gold ingots.
- Monster HP multiplier: level 1 x1, level 2 x1.22, level 3 x1.44, level 4 x1.66, level 5 x1.88

## Chest coins

- The deeper the level, the more coins in chests (base 8 + a value that scales with level + 0–19).

## Achievements

- Going Underground, Bottom of the Abyss (level 5) and Undersea Exploration are the dungeon achievements.

beaconfall/villages-trading.b:
:: Village NPCs = 6
:: Cottages = 3, 350 coins each
:: Prosperity ranks = 5
:: Max discount = 20% (Village Benefactor)
:: Haggling patience = 3
:: Trading Post buyers = NPCs

The Village Island is a safe island with no monsters. One of the Forest Islands becomes the village, with NPCs, shops and cottages.

You can also build Villager Houses on your own island and grow a settlement of your own. See the Settlement & Villagers page.

## Village NPCs

- **Bor the Blacksmith**: Gear and ingots
- **Mina the Farmer**: Seeds, food, carts, horses
- **Toby the Shopkeeper**: Basic materials and furniture
- **Haru the Sailor**: Boats, fishing rods, potions, runs the fishing tournament
- **Ria the Librarian**: Recipe books
- **Dowin the Village Chief**: Village prosperity and daily bonus

## Shop lists (prices in coins)

- Bor: Iron Longsword 110, Iron Pickaxe 110, Iron Axe 100, Iron Bow 100 / Gold Longsword 340, Gold Pickaxe 340, Gold Bow 320 / bundle of 8 arrows 16 / bundle of 6 feather arrows 54 / iron, copper and zinc ingots 30, gold ingot 90
- Mina: Seeds 8, sapling 10, bread 14, stew 36, milk 12, grilled fish 22, egg 8, string 6, cart 250 (Resident rank or higher), horse 500 (Neighbor rank or higher)
- Toby: Planks 5, bundle of 2 branches 2, bundle of 4 stone 5, log 4, leather 14, string 6, chest 30, bed 60
- Haru: Boat 240, Island Map 140, fishing rods 40, 130 and 400, Fire Resistance Potion 120, Antidote 40, Cactus Juice 30, bundle of 18 arrows 8

## Buying books (Ria the Librarian)

- Intro to Mechanical Engineering 150
- Signals & Circuits 220
- Gourmet Cookbook 90
- Compression Alchemy 180
- Books have to be bought separately for each save (world).

## Cottages

- There are 3, at 350 coins each. Buying one makes its bed your respawn point.

## Prosperity

As your prosperity score goes up, your rank goes up.

- Visitor 0, Resident 100, Neighbor 300, Honorary Resident 700, Village Benefactor 1500
- Purchase discounts: Visitor 0%; Resident, Neighbor and Honorary Resident 10%; Village Benefactor 20%
- Selling bonus: Honorary Resident +10%, Village Benefactor +15%
- Village chief's daily bonus coins: Neighbor 20, Honorary Resident 20, Village Benefactor 50
- Your score goes up from donating coins (1 point per coin), buying (money spent / 15), selling (money earned / 30) and donating items.

## Haggling

- You can haggle with merchants, and it resets daily. They have 3 patience.
- Asking for 10%, 20% or 30% off succeeds 70%, 45% or 25% of the time, varying slightly by merchant and prosperity rank.

## Selling prices

- Fish: 4, 10, 24 and 60 by tier
- Ingots: 12–36
- Crystal: 40

## Wandering merchants

- **Merchant Ship**: Arrives near the camp dock every 3 days after 7 AM. Bring it the items it wants and it gives rewards based on rarity.
- **Wandering Market (Kuro)**: Opens every 3 days on a random island other than the Village and Pirate Islands. It offers 7 random picks from 18 rare items, and buys fish at 1.5x.

## Player trading facilities

- **Trading Post**: Every 25 seconds, an NPC customer comes by and buys stocked goods at 1.15x x a distance multiplier (up to 1.8). Up to 6 item types, 300 stock and 3000 coins in stored cash. The farther away you build it, the more you earn. Unlike what the older pages said, it sells to NPCs, not other players.
- **Market Stall**: Sells to other players. Up to 6 item types, 99 of each; the default price is 1.5x the selling price, and you can change it yourself.
- **Mailbox**: Up to 10 letters, 60 characters each, up to 3 gift types. Delivery takes 15–240 seconds (depending on distance), and only the owner can read them.
- **Guestbook Stone**: Up to 12 entries, 40 characters, one per name

## Cargo Port

- Made from 1 boat, 1 Circuit Board and 2 Reinforced Brass Plates (requires Intro to Mechanical Engineering).
- A ship carries cargo fed in by conveyor to another Cargo Port on the same frequency.
- About halfway through the trip, pirates attack and take half the cargo. A Guard Post (needs 5 arrows loaded) or insurance prevents this.
- Guard Posts have 110 range and deal 4 damage.

## Coin-earning tips

- When you visit the Village Island, claim your Journal rewards and join the fishing tournament.
- Smelting ore into ingots adds a lot of value.
- Try haggling before making unnecessary purchases.

beaconfall/transportation.b:
:: Walking speed = 50
:: Horse = x1.9, 500 coins
:: Boat = Speed 80, 240 coins
:: Cart = 21 slots, 250 coins
:: Hot air balloon = 120-second flight
:: Ghost Ship = Night sea, 55% per day

Here's how to get between islands, plus the events that roam the world.

## Walking and speed

- Walking speed 50
- River water x0.6, mangrove x0.8
- Swiftness Potion +15%
- Horse x1.9, cart x0.92, boat 80, hot air balloon 72

## Boats

- Made from 5 planks and 2 iron ingots (also sold in the village for 240 coins).
- Hold it and press Shift at the water's edge to board. Press Shift or F to get off.
